info.name: Folio API
info.description:
**Signing in.** Each operation's `security` says what it takes:

- **Bearer token or cookie** (the default: `GET /api/tokens`, `POST /api/tokens/{tokenId}`, `GET /api/me` and
  the three shelves endpoints): exchange a username and password for a token at `POST /api/tokens`, then send
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. With that header present it alone decides; the cookie is no fallback.
- **Session cookie only** (`security: [sessionCookie: []]`): everything else under `/account`, plus
  `POST /confirm-email` and `POST /read/{book}/ask`. A bearer token is ignored there, so a request with only a
  token is signed out (401 without `WWW-Authenticate`, or a 303 or 302 to `/login`). The cookie comes from the
  `POST /login` form, `POST /passkeys/sign-in` (a passkey) or finishing a sign-up at `POST /signup`.
- **Cookie optional** (`security: [{}, sessionCookie: []]`): `POST /logout`, and `GET /offline/{file}`, where a
  catalogue book is anyone's and a private one needs its owner's cookie.
- **Public** (`security: []`): `POST /api/tokens` (it takes the password itself), the sign-in, sign-up and
  password-reset forms, the passkey sign-in, public files, the manifest and the health check.
- **Signed webhooks**: `POST /billing/paddle` (`paddleSignature`) and `POST /mail/events`
  (`resendSvixSignature`) take no account; each checks an HMAC signature over the raw body instead.

A cookie request that changes something must come from Folio's own origin (`Origin`, or `Sec-Fetch-Site:
same-origin`), else a plain-text 403. Admin-only operations answer a member with 404, so a member learns nothing.

**Gates and limits** are on each operation as vendor extensions, and in its description: `x-admin-only`,
`x-pro-feature` (Free gets 403 `pro`, or a form's `?error=pro`), `x-rate-limit`, `x-quota` (with the Free and Pro
numbers) and `x-outside-services` (Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Wikimedia, Open Library, Paddle, Resend).

**Form posts.** Pages that are also form targets (`/login`, `/signup`, `/account`, `/account/api-keys` and others)
take `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `multipart/form-data` and answer with a `303` whose `Location` carries
the outcome (`?status=…` or `?error=…`); only the post is described here, not the HTML page. The form handlers set
no byte cap, ignore fields they don't use and read a missing field as empty: the form schemas are what Folio's
own pages send.

**JSON bodies** are `Content-Type: application/json` (else 415) under each operation's size cap (else 413).
Unknown fields and wrong types are refused with 400 `invalid`, never ignored. Uploads of a private book's
chapters, pictures, cover and audiobook files are raw bodies, step by step, as each operation says.

**Errors** are JSON `{ "error": "<code>" }` (the `Error` schema, or a schema of its own when the body carries
more), except a foreign `Origin`, which is a plain-text 403, and the file and download routes, which answer
plain text. The private book import's first steps use hyphenated codes (`signed-out`, `not-found`).

**Caching.** Every JSON answer about an account is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. A request that carries a
session cookie gets `private, no-store` on every answer, public files included (src/start.ts).

**Another account's** token, shelf, book, highlight or other record is a 404 `not_found`, never a 403.

item.name: Sign in with a username and password (the sign-in form)

request.description:
A plain HTML form post, answered with a `303`. Every refusal, whatever the reason (wrong password; unknown,
disabled or malformed username; a password over 1,024 characters; a locked username; a blocked IP), is the
same `error=invalid`, so nobody learns which accounts exist. The attempt is recorded as a failure before the
password is checked, so parallel requests can't slip past the limits; an unknown or disabled username is
still checked against a dummy hash, so timing reveals nothing.

On success any session the request's cookie still names is ended, a new 30-day session starts (it also ends
after 7 days without use), and the browser goes to `next`. `next` is followed only when it is a same-site path
(`src/shared/lib/safe-next.ts`): it starts with `/` but not `//` or `/\`, has no scheme, backslash or control
characters, is at most 1,000 characters and still is a same-site path after URL normalisation. Anything else,
or none, is `/library`.

A foreign `Origin` header is 403; without `Origin` the request needs `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. The cookie
sent with the request plays no part beyond being replaced. Answers are `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

response.name:
Signed in: `Location` is `next` (as `safeNext` returned it), or `/library`, with the new session in
  `Set-Cookie`.
- `/login?error=invalid`: the body isn't a form, or the username and password don't sign in (any reason
  above, limits included).
- `/login?error=unavailable`: no database is configured, or something failed on the server (logged).

Both error targets add `&next=<the safe next path, URL-encoded>` unless it is `/library`, for example
`/login?error=invalid&next=%2Faccount`. No `Set-Cookie` on an error.

item.name: Ask for a sign-up link, or finish a sign-up from a link (the sign-up forms)

request.description:
One handler for `/signup`'s two forms, told apart by the `token` field: a form with `token` finishes a sign-up,
anything else asks for a link. Plain form posts answered with `303`.

**Asking for a link** (only when the server's `SIGNUP` mode is `open`). Every answer that isn't about the
request itself is `status=sent`, at once: an address that already has accounts, a bounced one, one over its 3
links a day, and a filled honeypot (`website`) all get it. The link is made and mailed (through Resend) after
the response, so neither the answer nor its timing says anything about the address. A sign-up link works once,
for 24 hours; the account it makes has the address already confirmed.

**Finishing** (an invite in `invite` or `open` mode, a mailed link only in `open` mode). The link is checked,
then the username (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{2,31}$` after trimming and lowercasing; a reserved name such as
`admin` is refused as `taken`), then the password policy, then the confirmation. Each refusal counts against
the link, which dies at the 10th. The account is a `member`, made in one transaction (one link makes one
account), and is signed in at once: any session the cookie named is ended and a new one set. An invite works
once, for 7 days.

A signed-in visitor can do neither. A foreign `Origin` header is 403; without `Origin` the request needs
`Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. Answers carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and
`Referrer-Policy: strict-origin`.

response.name:
Asking for a link (no `token` field):

- `/signup`: sign-up isn't `open`, or the visitor is signed in.
- `/signup?status=sent`: accepted (or quietly not sent; see above). Also a filled honeypot.
- `/signup?error=invalid`: not an address (or not a form).
- `/signup?error=limited`: 5 requests in the last hour from this IP.
- `/signup?error=busy`: the site has made 30 sign-up links in the last 24 hours.
- `/signup?error=unavailable`: the database is down or not configured.

Finishing (`token` field; `T` is the token):

- `/signup`: the token isn't 43 base64url characters.
- `/signup?token=T`: sign-up is `off`, the visitor is signed in, or the link isn't live (unknown, used,
  expired, revoked, killed by refusals) or its kind isn't allowed in this mode. The page says which.
- `/signup?token=T&error=username&username=U`: the username doesn't match the pattern.
- `/signup?token=T&error=taken&username=U`: the username is reserved or already taken.
- `/signup?token=T&error=policy&reason=short|long|username&username=U`: the password is under 15 or over
  256 characters, or is the username.
- `/signup?token=T&error=mismatch&username=U`: `confirm` isn't `password`.
- `/signup?token=T&error=unavailable`: a field is over 1,024 characters; with `&username=U` when
  something failed on the server.
- `/account?status=welcome`: the account was made and signed in; `Set-Cookie` carries the session.

`U` is the lowercased username, cut to 32 characters, URL-encoded. The password is never in `Location`.

request.description:
One plain HTML form post, its `intent` field choosing the action. Every answer is a `303` with no body, back
to `/account` with a `status` or `error` code (and a fragment naming the page's section), so it works without
JavaScript. The page maps each code to fixed text. Fields the intent doesn't use are ignored, and a missing
field reads as an empty string.

Order of checks: a foreign `Origin` (or, without one, no `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`) is 403 before
anything else; then no session cookie, or one naming no live session (or a failed lookup), goes to
`/login?next=%2Faccount`; then a body that isn't a form is `?error=invalid`; then the intent. An unknown or
missing intent is `?error=invalid`. A database failure inside an intent is `?error=unavailable`.

What each intent answers:

- `change-password`: `password` and `confirm` differ → `?error=mismatch#password`; the new password breaks
  the policy → `?error=policy&reason=<short|long|username>#password` (fewer than 15 or more than 256
  characters after NFC, or the username itself, case ignored); the current password is wrong, over 1,024
  characters, or the username is locked → `?error=current#password` (checked in that order, so only the last
  check counts towards the lock). Success → `?status=password-changed`: the hash is replaced, every other
  session and every access token of the account end, and this session's cookie stays as it is.
- `revoke-others`: ends every other session and every access token → `?status=signed-out-others#sessions`.
- `token-revoke`: `token` is a token id. Another account's id, or one that isn't a UUID, gets the same answer
  and changes nothing → `?status=token-revoked#access-tokens`.
- `passkey-remove`: `passkey` is a passkey id (case ignored). No password asked. Another account's id, or a
  malformed one, gets the same answer and changes nothing → `?status=passkey-removed#passkeys`.
- `delete-account`: wrong or locked current password → `?error=delete-current#delete`; the account is the only
  enabled admin → `?error=last-admin#delete`; billing is on and Paddle couldn't cancel a subscription that
  can still bill → `?error=delete-billing#delete`. Otherwise the account and everything in it are deleted
  (an account that was already gone answers the same) → `/login?status=account-deleted` with a `Set-Cookie`
  that clears the session cookie. This is the only intent that sets a cookie.
- `email-add`, `email-resend`, `email-remove`: with mail off (no mail settings or no database) every one
  answers `/account#email` and touches nothing.
  - `email-add`: an address `parseEmail` refuses → `?error=email-invalid#email` (before the password is
    checked); wrong or locked current password → `?error=email-current#email`; it is already the confirmed,
    unbounced address → `?error=email-same#email`; 5 links in the last hour → `?error=email-limit#email`;
    the mail is refused (Resend 400/422) → `?error=email-invalid#email`; Resend 429 → `?error=email-busy#email`;
    any other send failure → `?error=email-failed#email`. A failed send leaves the earlier pending address in
    place. Sent → `?status=email-sent#email`; the link, valid 24 hours, replaces any older pending one.
  - `email-resend`: nothing pending, or the pending address bounced → `/account#email`; otherwise a new link to
    the pending address, with `email-add`'s limit and send outcomes (`email-limit`, `email-invalid`,
    `email-busy`, `email-failed`, `email-sent`).
  - `email-remove`: with `pending=1` drops only the pending address → `/account#email`; otherwise clears the
    confirmed address and every unused link → `?status=email-removed#email`.

A current-password re-check (`change-password`, `delete-account`, `email-add`) is recorded as a sign-in
attempt for the username: a failure counts towards the username's lock and the IP's block on `/login`, and
while the username is locked every re-check fails without checking the password (audited as `login.locked`).

response.name:
Back to the page with the outcome (see the operation's description for which intent answers what), or to
`/login` when signed out or after deleting the account. No body.

item.name: Save, replace or delete a provider API key, or choose the agent or voice model

request.description:
One plain HTML form post, its `intent` field choosing the action. Every answer is a `303` with no body, back
to `/account/api-keys` with a `status` or `error` code; a key's answer also carries `provider=` and the
provider's section as the fragment, so the page shows the outcome there. No answer sets a cookie.

Order of checks: a foreign `Origin` (or, without one, no `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`) is 403; then no live
session goes to `/login?next=%2Faccount%2Fapi-keys`; then a body that isn't a form is `?error=invalid`.

- `model` (the model Ask the book uses with the Anthropic key): an id not in the list → `?error=invalid#model`;
  saved → `?status=model-saved#model`; a database failure → `?error=failed#model`. Not counted against the
  key limit, and not a Pro check.
- `speech-model` (the ElevenLabs voice model for read aloud): the same, answered with
  `?<code>&provider=elevenlabs#speech-model` (`error=invalid`, `status=speech-model-saved`, `error=failed`).
- Anything else needs `provider` to be `anthropic` or `elevenlabs`, else `?error=invalid` (no provider, no
  fragment). Then the key limit: 10 `api_key.saved`, `api_key.deleted` and `api_key.rejected` events in the
  last hour, both providers together, answer `error=limit` for every intent below, deletes included. Then:
  - `save`: ElevenLabs on Free → `error=pro`. The key is trimmed, then shape-checked before anything leaves the
    server: Anthropic needs `sk-ant-`, 20–300 characters, no whitespace (`error=shape`); ElevenLabs needs
    20–300 characters, no whitespace (`error=shape`), and not an `sk-ant-` key (`error=anthropic`). Then the
    provider checks it (10 s, no redirects): Anthropic `GET {ANTHROPIC_API_BASE}/v1/models?limit=1` with
    `x-api-key`, ElevenLabs `GET {ELEVENLABS_API_BASE}/v2/voices?page_size=1` with `xi-api-key`. 200 saves it
    → `status=saved`; Anthropic 401/403 or ElevenLabs 401 → `error=rejected`; ElevenLabs 403 (the key can't
    read voices) → `error=permission` (both audited as `api_key.rejected`, so they count towards the limit);
    any other status, a timeout or a network error → `error=unavailable`. Saving replaces any earlier key of
    that provider.
  - `delete`: deletes the provider's key, if there is one (on Free too) → `status=deleted`.
  - any other intent → `error=invalid`.
  - a database failure, or no KEK configured (after the provider accepted the key) → `error=failed`.

What is stored: the key encrypted with AES-256-GCM under the server's KEK (a fresh 12-byte IV, the auth tag,
the KEK's id, associated data binding it to the account and provider), its last 4 characters, and when it was
saved and checked. The key is never sent back; the page shows only the last 4 characters.

response.name: Back to the page with the outcome (see the operation's description), or to `/login`. No body.

request.description:
The browser reads the book file itself (EPUB, PDF, Markdown or a ZIP of Markdown; the file is never uploaded)
and sends structured blocks, never HTML. An import is four kinds of request, all linked by the `id` this one
answers:

1. **This request**: the metadata, the four optional details, `chapterCount` and the pictures that will
   follow (`images.count` and their bytes in all). It sweeps the account's imports still uploading after 24
   hours, checks the limits with the account locked, and makes an `uploading` book. Then, optionally, the
   cover: `POST /account/books/{id}/cover?source=epub|zip|pdf`.
2. `POST /account/books/{id}/images/{n}` once for each picture `n` from 1 to `images.count`.
3. `POST /account/books/{id}/chapters/{position}` once for each chapter `position` from 0 to
   `chapterCount - 1`; a chapter may show only pictures already stored.
4. `POST /account/books/{id}/finish` once every chapter and picture has arrived; it marks the book ready.

An import never finished is deleted at the account's next import after 24 hours. Error codes on these four
endpoints are hyphenated (`not-found`, `signed-out`), unlike the rest of the API.

Checks, in order: the origin (403), the session (401), the body (415, 413, 400), then the store: the hourly
import limit (429), the plan's book limit (409 `books`), the account's picture room (409 `user`).

feature (404), the server's free disk (409 `server`), then, with the account locked: the hourly import limit

goes wrong arrives as an `error` event in the stream.

`active`, `trialing` and `past_due` are Pro, `paused` and `canceled` Free.

One change per request, chosen by `intent`:

- `reset-password`: a new generated password (in the answer once, as for Add). The account's passkeys go in

- `disable`: ends every session and access token. 409 `last_admin` for the only enabled admin. Disabling a

- `enable`: never refused.
- `unlock`: clears the username's sign-in failures, which ends the lock.
- `sign-out`: ends every session and access token.
- `role` (with `role`): holds from the account's next request. 409 `last_admin` when it would demote the only

- `grant-pro` / `revoke-pro`: give or take back Pro; 409 `admin` on an admin, who is always Pro. Granting
  again, or revoking a grant that isn't there, is a 200 that changes nothing.
- `delete`: the account and everything that is theirs. A subscription that could still bill them is
  cancelled at Paddle first, at once; when Paddle can't be reached the account isn't deleted (502

member; 404 for a malformed username, before any query; the body (1 KB; 415, 413 or 400 `invalid`) and its
fields (400 `invalid`); 404 for an unknown username; 409 `self` for the admin's own account, which is changed
